tradeoffs.observed: Summarizer is mounted at a static route `/chat/summarizer` beside Prompt’s `/chat`, while `/chat/[id]` remains Prompt-only.
tradeoffs.tradeoff: A named static segment is clear and wins over `[id]` in the App Router. As more Built-in AI demos land, either `/chat/<api>` proliferates with repeated page shells, or conversation IDs and API type collide under one dynamic segment without a richer route model.

options.gains: Matches Prompt’s shallow routing today; no conversation/API model required.
options.costs: Each new API needs another static page and PlusIcon shell; conversation history cannot distinguish API type.

options.move: Make a type boundary explicit so downstream branching disappears
options.gains: A single chat route keyed by API id (or typed conversation records) scales without one folder per API.
options.costs: Needs a routing/data model before Writer/Rewriter exist, and more upfront wiring than a static page.

tradeoffs.question: How should additional Built-in AI demos be routed relative to `/chat` and `/chat/[id]`?

tradeoffs.observed: SummarizerApiDemo is a near-copy of PromptApiDemo’s status machine, download monitor, abort/cleanup, and Generate/Stop UI, with Summarizer-specific create options and summarizeStreaming.
tradeoffs.tradeoff: Shipping a second full demo keeps each API page self-contained and matches the plan’s YAGNI stance. The same lifecycle now lives in two ~200-line components (fallow reports 5 clone groups / 104 shared lines), so a third API would multiply that cost.

options.gains: No shared abstraction to design yet; Summarizer can diverge (type/length/format) without negotiating a common shell.
options.costs: Lifecycle and UI fixes must be applied twice; Writer/Rewriter will likely add more clones.

options.move: Extract a helper, or split a large file into focused modules
options.gains: One place owns availability → download → stream → abort; API demos only supply create/run adapters and option fields.
options.costs: Requires designing a shared contract now for only two callers, and may overfit Prompt+Summarizer.

tradeoffs.question: Under what conditions should the Prompt and Summarizer demo lifecycle be shared versus kept duplicated?

tradeoffs.observed: Each Summarize click creates a new Summarizer session with the current type/format/length, streams, then leaves cleanup to stop/next run (destroy on cleanup).
tradeoffs.tradeoff: Recreating on every run always applies the latest option selects and matches Chrome’s “options fixed at create” rule. Holding a long-lived session would avoid re-download/create cost when options are unchanged, but would require invalidating the session when type/length/format change.

options.gains: Option changes always take effect; no session/option sync bugs.
options.costs: Repeated create overhead on every Summarize, including when options did not change.

options.gains: A retained session can be reused when options are unchanged and recreated only when they change.
options.costs: Session lifecycle and option-diff logic become another state machine to maintain.

tradeoffs.question: When should a Summarizer session be reused across Summarize clicks versus created fresh each time?
